sections.h2: Where is the Cocke County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office sits inside the Newport courthouse at 111 Court Avenue, Newport, TN 37821. Come on a weekday between 8:00 and 4:30, or on a Saturday morning between 8:00 and 11:00.

Reach it by phone at (423) 623-7540, by fax at (423) 623-7556, or by email at ccrod@cockecountytn.gov. The county's Register of Deeds page carries the staff list and the fee schedule.

A deed that transfers a Cocke County house has to be recorded here before it enters the public record. Your closing agent normally delivers it, though an owner can also bring the paper in person.

One rule covers warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, judgments, restrictions, agreements and amendments. It charges $5.00 per page with a $10.00 floor, then adds a $2.00 data processing fee. The charge rests on Tennessee Code 8-21-1001.

Cocke County recording fees by document type
Document typeFee
Deed, deed of trust, lease, lien, judgment, restriction, agreement or amendment$5.00 a page, $10.00 floor, plus a $2.00 processing fee
Release of one lien$10.00 covers the first two pages, $2.00 processing, then $5.00 for each added page and deed reference
Assignment or modification$10.00 for one assignment on one or two pages plus $2.00, then $5.00 per extra page or reference
Fixture filing$15.00, plus $15.00 per additional indexed party (spouses count as two names)
Charter$5.00 through five pages plus $2.00, then 50 cents a page
Certified copy$1.00 plus $1.00 for every page

The preparer's name and address must appear on everything except releases and charters. Assignments and modifications also have to recite the maximum principal indebtedness for recording tax purposes, though $0 is an acceptable figure.

sections.h2: State transfer tax on a Cocke County sale
sections.html:
Tennessee's levy is $3.70 per $1,000, or 37 cents per $100 in the state's own wording. Think of it as the price of moving title: every real property transfer owes it, and the base is usually the greater of the sale price and the property's value. Cocke County also charges a $1.00 probate fee, collected only when state tax is paid.

New debt secured by the property triggers a second levy, the indebtedness tax. The county lists it at $1.15 per $1,000 with the first $2,000 exempt, which the state help page gives as $0.115 per $100. Both taxes trace to Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. Your closing agent will total them for the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What register staff will and will not do
sections.html:
Clerks accept filings, index them and make copies. Drafting is outside their role. The office may not write documents or run title searches, since its people are neither bonded nor attorneys.

That matters if you inherited the house or plan to sell without an agent. A title company or lawyer writes the deed and reviews ownership history, and the register's role begins once the instrument is signed.

The register also runs an email alert system. Enter a first and last name plus an email address on the site the county links to, and any later recording under that name sends you a message. It is useful for a house you are about to sell or for land you rarely visit, since a forged deed would trigger a message right away.

Cocke County had an estimated 37,889 residents in July 2025, a 5.3% rise from the 35,999 counted in April 2020. A typical owner-occupied home was worth $158,100 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, rent in the middle of the market was $798 a month, and owners filled 74.5% of housing. Newport serves as county seat and largest city. Parrottsville is the one other incorporated town.

sections.h2: Who bills the property tax on a Cocke County house?
sections.html:
Tennessee's calendar sets the assessment date at January 1. The payment window opens on the first Monday in October. A balance still open after the final day of February is delinquent.

The register records deeds and does not bill property tax. Two calls help before closing. The Cocke County Trustee can give a payoff on the parcel, and the Assessor of Property can give its appraised value and classification. The title company needs both numbers for its settlement statement.

If you dispute a value, the general deadline to reach the State Board of Equalization is August 1, or 45 days after the county board sends its notice, whichever is later. Ask the closing agent to match the deed's legal description to the parcel before recording.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Take the original signed and notarized deed, plus the names and addresses of both parties and of the preparer, and your payment. Confirm how the office accepts payment before you make the trip.

  • The deed, with the preparer's name and address shown on it.
  • The price or value, so staff can compute the transfer tax.
  • Money covering the page charge, the $2.00 processing fee and $3.70 per $1,000 of tax.
  • For a release, the lien details and deed book reference, as each extra reference is $5.00.

For an unusual document, call (423) 623-7540 or send an email to confirm charges first.

sections.h2: A typical sale from signing to recording
sections.html:
Most Cocke County sellers never touch the recording step themselves. After signing and notarizing, the closing agent verifies the preparer's name and address are on the deed, totals what the register will charge, and carries the package to Court Avenue.

Once staff index the deed, the sale shows in the public record. For proof of the filing, order a certified copy, which is $1.00 plus $1.00 for every page. If your name is on the alert list, a message arrives when the new deed is filed, which confirms the filing went through.

sections.h2: If you are selling an inherited or family house
sections.html:
Heirs and family sellers often reach the Register's counter without a deed prepared. Because the staff cannot write documents, the first stop should be a title company or attorney who can review ownership history and draft the deed. Only then does the signed paper come here for recording.

Before you list, ask the Trustee whether any tax year is open. Clear tax records and a deed that fits the parcel help a buyer's lender sign off, and they protect your closing date.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Cocke County?
faqs.a: Expect $5.00 per page, a $10.00 minimum and a $2.00 data processing fee. The county website lists the full schedule for other document types.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Cocke County house sale?
faqs.a: Cocke County lists the state tax at $3.70 per $1,000, which equals 37 cents per $100, usually applied to whichever is higher, the price or the value. The Department of Revenue points to Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409 for it.

faqs.q: Can the Cocke County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office may not prepare documents or perform title searches, because staff are neither bonded nor attorneys. Ask a title company or attorney to write the deed; the register then records it.

faqs.q: Is the Cocke County Register of Deeds open on Saturday?
faqs.a: Yes, Saturday mornings from 8:00 to 11:00. Weekday hours run 8:00 to 4:30. Call (423) 623-7540 or visit 111 Court Avenue in Newport.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether anyone recorded a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Sign up for the register's email alert on the site the county links to. You give your name and an email address, and every later recording under that name sends you a message. You can also call the office about a specific filing.
